item.title: Trump leaves stage mid-speech to embrace parents of 12-year-old killed by stray bullet in the Bronx
item.description: President Donald Trump left the stage mid-speech at the Nassau County Police Academy to embrace the parents of Jacob Freytes, a 12-year-old killed by a stray bullet.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump stepped off the stage on Friday while making a speech in New York to comfort the family of a 12-year-old boy who was killed by a stray bullet in the Bronx.

Trump was speaking to the Nassau County Police Academy when he mentioned Jacob Freytes, a boy who was killed late last month by a stray bullet while sitting on his bike outside a bodega.

"In a beautiful impromptu moment, President Trump exits the stage in the middle of his speech to embrace Migdalia Martinez and retired NYPD Sergeant Jesus Freytes, whose 12-year-old son Jacob was tragically killed by a stray bullet in the Bronx," White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt wrote on social media after capturing the moment on video.

CRIME IS FALLING, OFFICIALS SAY — VICTIMS CLAIM REPORTING ISN’T WORTH IT

Before leaving the stage to meet his parents, Trump mentioned Freytes while talking about his administration’s effort to lower crime.

"Two weeks ago, a 12-year-old boy named Jacob Freytes — You read about this one? — was tragically shot and killed by a stray bullet fired by a repeat offender in a gun battle."

He added: "Jacob was the son of a loving mom and a retired New York City police detective, and they are incredible people, and I think I heard that they may be with us today. Are you with us?"

He then left the stage and hugged Freytes' teary-eyed mom, Migdalia Martinez, and his father, retired NYPD Sgt. Jesus Freytes, saying a few private words to both of them.

AS SOCIALIST MAYOR BATTLES ICE, SEATTLE POLICE AND CRIME VICTIMS SAY REPEAT OFFENDERS ARE TERRORIZING THE CITY

"Incredible. Horrible story. What a horrible thing," he said when he returned to the stage. "But we're going after them. These are bad, sick people."

Freytes’ death has prompted Republicans to introduce "Jacob’s Law" in the New York Legislature that would put harsher penalties on criminals whose reckless actions result in the death of a child.

"I gave him a kiss, and I walked out, and we always do a little dolphin kiss. And I walked out and went to work," Martinez told "Fox & Friends" Tuesday.

"Around five o'clock, they called me and said that he had gotten shot. And all I could do was try to think of different ways to get here faster," she added. "When I got there, I just seen my boy gone."

Police said William Ferrer, 45, was arrested and faces multiple charges, including second-degree murder. He has pleaded not guilty. Ferrer has an arrest record dating back more than 25 years, including prior charges for drunk driving, drug possession, menacing and criminal contempt, according to the New York Post.

Fox News' Madison Colombo contributed to this report.

item.title: FBI captures Top Ten Most Wanted fugitive with alleged Sinaloa Cartel ties, Patel says
item.description: Gregory Henderson Jr. was captured three days after being added to the FBI Ten Most Wanted list for alleged drug trafficking tied to the Sinaloa Cartel.
item.content:encoded:
The FBI captured Ten Most Wanted fugitive Gregory Henderson Jr., just three days after adding the alleged Indianapolis gang leader to its list and offering a reward of up to $1 million for information leading to his arrest.

Henderson, 46, had evaded arrest since a sweeping federal takedown of his alleged organization in August 2023. He faces federal charges of conspiracy to possess with intent to distribute and to distribute controlled substances, conspiracy to launder monetary instruments and conspiracy to engage in an animal fighting venture.

The FBI alleges Henderson led a violent Indianapolis gang whose drug trafficking network was supplied by the Sinaloa Cartel and distributed methamphetamine, cocaine and fentanyl throughout Indianapolis and the surrounding Midwest.

WOMAN ADDED TO FBI'S TEN MOST WANTED LIST ARRESTED HOURS LATER AFTER TIPS POURED IN FROM FLORIDA: PATEL

His capture marks the ninth FBI Ten Most Wanted fugitive apprehended since President Donald Trump returned to office. The nine fugitives had collectively spent more than 50 years on the run, according to the FBI. The FBI says the nine captures are more than twice the four Ten Most Wanted fugitives captured during the Biden administration.

FBI Director Kash Patel told Fox News Digital exclusively that Henderson’s capture reflected a broader increase in Ten Most Wanted apprehensions under the Trump administration.

"Nine Top Ten Most Wanted Fugitives is more than twice as many as captured under the entirety of the prior administration — and this FBI and our partners did it in 18 months under President Trump’s brilliant leadership," Patel said. "Gregory Henderson Jr. had been on the run for a year, wanted for his alleged involvement in major drug trafficking operation and animal fighting conspiracies as the alleged leader of a violent neighborhood-based gang located in Indianapolis, Indiana - a gang with significant drug distribution ties to the Sinaloa Cartel."

"This administration is letting good cops be cops and they are delivering in historic ways. I’d like to congratulate our FBI Indianapolis team who led this case from the beginning and thank our great Justice Department and law enforcement partners who righteously pursued this case with us," he added.

'AMERICA'S MOST WANTED' FUGITIVE CAPTURED ON SAILBOAT OFF NJ COAST AFTER 20 YEARS ON THE RUN

The U.S. Department of Agriculture’s Office of Inspector General was among the federal partners involved in the case.

"I would like to thank the FBI, DOJ, and our USDA OIG among many other federal partners in their relentless pursuit for justice. Mr. Henderson had sought to evade the law after committing multiple crimes and leaving behind pain and anguish for many people and animals, but today is the end of that devastation," U.S. Secretary of Agriculture Brooke L. Rollins told Fox News Digital "President Trump has focused his administration on delivering justice for those targeted by violent crimes, and we will not rest until we achieve this goal."

The FBI added Henderson to its Ten Most Wanted Fugitives list on Aug. 11, describing him as armed and dangerous.

Henderson and 20 others were federally indicted in the Southern District of Indiana in August 2023 on drug trafficking and dog fighting conspiracy charges. More than 300 federal, state and local law enforcement officers carried out a takedown later that month, arresting 18 people while Henderson evaded capture.

Federal agents seized 61 guns, quantities of fentanyl, methamphetamine and cocaine, $98,000 in cash and 166 fighting dogs during the operation, according to the FBI.

Law enforcement also uncovered what the FBI described as a significant dog fighting and illegal gambling operation allegedly led by Henderson.

"Henderson Jr. has a long history of criminal activity, including street violence, intimidation, assault, and weapons, in addition to drug trafficking and animal cruelty," said FBI Indianapolis Special Agent in Charge Tim O’Malley.

Details about where and how Henderson was captured were not immediately available.

item.title: Teenage British cyclist Finlay Tarling dies after tragic incident in Volta a Portugal race
item.description: Finlay Tarling, 19, was struck by a car that reportedly entered the road during stage 8 of the Volta a Portugal and died, his NSN Cycling Team announced.
item.content:encoded:
Teenage British cyclist Finlay Tarling died Friday following a tragic incident in the Volta a Portugal race, NSN Cycling Team announced to social media.

Tarling, 19, was run over by a car that entered the road, according to local reports. The driver reportedly missed the signs from stewards and entered the road going in the opposite direction of the race.

"We are heartbroken to announce the passing of Finlay Tarling at the Volta a Portugal today," NSN Cycling Team said on X. "Fin was a much loved member of our team but most importantly, he was a son, a brother, and a friend to so many. He will be deeply missed."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

The incident occurred during the eighth stage of the race, between Melgaço and Fafe in northern Portugal. Tarling was immediately attended to by doctors. It wasn’t clear if other riders were involved.

"At this moment of profound dismay, the organization of the Volta a Portugal and the Portuguese Cycling Federation express their most heartfelt condolences to the family of Finlay Tarling, to his teammates, to the NSN Development Team, and to all his friends and loved ones," organizers said on X.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

The eighth stage of the race was stopped following the incident "as a sign of respect and mourning," organizers added.

Portuguese President António José Seguro and Portuguese Prime Minister Luís Montenegro both sent messages of condolence to the rider's family.

Tarling was the younger brother of Ineos Grenadiers cyclist Joshua Tarling. Tarling represented Great Britain on the road and track. He placed second in Stage 6 of the Tour du Rwanda earlier this year.

item.title: Stephen A Smith admits Byron Donalds could make him a Republican, calls him ‘the real deal’
item.description: Stephen A. Smith says Byron Donalds could make him a Republican, praising the Trump-backed Florida gubernatorial frontrunner ahead of the GOP primary.
item.content:encoded:
ESPN host Stephen A. Smith said Thursday that Rep. Byron Donalds, R-Fla., could make him a Republican, praising the Trump-backed gubernatorial frontrunner days before Florida Republicans choose their nominee to succeed Gov. Ron DeSantis.

"And I ain't no d--- Republican. But that mean if anybody could make me one, it would be him. I'm just going to keep it a buck. I'm just letting you know," Smith said.

"He's the real deal. Make no mistake about it. I've seen him battling with Democrats. I've seen him battling with people on different shows, whatever. He ain't backing up. He knows his stuff. OK? I talk to him all the time. All the time. And I ain't got nothing bad to say about him."

A Donalds campaign official confirmed to Fox News Digital Friday that Smith and Donalds are friends. Campaign communications director Gates McGavick said Donalds was attracting voters across demographic groups by focusing on affordability and public safety.

FLORIDA GOP GUBERNATORIAL PRIMARY CANDIDATE SAYS AS GOVERNOR, HE'D 'SHUT DOWN' EVERY ABORTION CLINIC IN STATE

"Byron Donalds is drawing support from Floridians of all backgrounds because he has a clear vision to make Florida more affordable, keep Floridians safe and make sure the radical left stays out of the Sunshine State," McGavick said. "He is building a broad coalition that puts common sense over crazy to lead Florida into the future."

One GOP source's assessment provided to Fox News Digital Friday focused on President Donald Trump's endorsement.

"Donalds is endorsed by POTUS, and we fully expect him to win the primary," the source said.

A James Madison Institute poll released Aug. 6 placed Donalds at 49% among likely Republican primary voters, 31 points ahead of Lt. Gov. Jay Collins. 

Donalds' campaign had raised more than $90 million while facing Collins, former Florida House Speaker Paul Renner and investor James Fishback as DeSantis withheld an endorsement of any candidate.

TRUMP FLEXES HIS POLITICAL MUSCLE OVER GOP AS DEMOCRATS SEE MIDTERM OPENING IN KEY RED STATE

Smith described himself as skeptical of Democrats while pressing Donalds on Black voters' distrust of Trump and concerns about Donalds' close alignment with the president.

"You heard me ask that question [What have Democrats done for you?]. I ain't apologizing for it. I'm very skeptical about them," Smith said.

"Make no mistake about it. I mean, I've lost interest in them in a lot of different ways. I'll be the first to admit it right here on the public airwaves, but I also am trying to be fair-minded when I think about this," he added.

The comments continue Smith's increasing openness to Republican candidates. In March, he challenged Democrats to earn Black votes rather than take them for granted. 

Days later, he told Sean Hannity that, despite being a Democrat, he would support Secretary of State Marco Rubio over prominent Democrats, including California Gov. Gavin Newsom and former Vice President Kamala Harris.

STEPHEN A. SMITH BLAMES ‘THE RIGHT’ FOR WNBA FIRESTORM, SAYS LEAGUE ‘LEFT THE DOOR OPEN’

Donalds answered Smith’s question about skepticism among Black voters by urging them to assess politicians through policies and results rather than personal comfort or social media commentary.

"It's something that I acknowledge. I would challenge Black people in America. First of all, this ain't even about trust. It's about verification," Donalds said.

"We've had people on both sides of the aisle promise Black people everything until the cows come home. But it's really about, 'Are you going to verify the promises and verify what the policies actually do, or are you just going to trust it because you have comfort level with a certain politician."

Fox News Digital reached out to Smith for comment but did not immediately receive a response.

DeSantis, who was re-elected in a landslide in 2022, is barred from running for a third term. Over the past 10 years, Florida has gone from being a swing state to being dominated by Republicans at the state and national levels.

item.title: Halle Berry celebrates 60th birthday in plunging robe with defiant message
item.description: Halle Berry marked her 60th birthday with a bold photo slideshow on Instagram, including a romantic shot with fiancé Van Hunt and selfies of her in a robe.
item.content:encoded:
Halle Berry is stepping into her 60s in style.

The "X-Men" actress shared a series of sultry photos on Instagram Thursday, the day before her birthday.

"Today….don’t give a f---!" she captioned the post.

In the photos, Berry posed for the camera in a black robe with large red floral designs and lace along the edges and sleeves.

EMILY RATAJKOWSKI'S SHREDDED RED BIRTHDAY DRESS LEAVES LITTLE TO THE IMAGINATION AT NYC CELEBRATION

She wore the robe tied loosely around her waist, creating a plunging neckline that extended down to her belly button and slightly exposed her chest.

Some of the photos show the "Monster's Ball" star indulging in chocolate-covered strawberries, while others show her smiling as she lounged on a daybed.

Fans sang Berry's praises in the comments.

"Not a single f--- left in stock!! Carry on, @halleberry! 🔥" one fan wrote.

Another added, "Why are you so perfect? Ugh 😍😍😍😍😍"

"Perfection! Queen ❤️," one commenter wrote, as another said, "My goodness… 🔥."

The actress also shared a photo kissing her fiancé, Van Hunt, as the two lounged on a sofa outside.

On Friday, Berry took to Instagram to thank all her followers for the birthday wishes with a picture of her holding up a card that said, "Happy 60th."

"Thank you from my ❤️ for all the birthday love and well wishes. I’m grateful to still be here!!" she wrote in the caption.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

Hunt and Berry began dating during the COVID-19 pandemic, and Berry told AARP: The Magazine in January 2022 they got to know each other for four months by talking on the phone.

"We were forced to let only our brains connect and discover if we had a connection before our bodies decided to get involved," she told the outlet. "I'd never done it this way. I fell in love with his mind, his conversation."

After sparking romance rumors in July 2020, Berry confirmed their relationship in September of that year with an Instagram photo of herself wearing a T-shirt with his name on it and the caption, "now ya know."

Since confirming their romance, the two have often been photographed together on the red carpet and have made frequent appearances on each other's social media accounts. Hunt revealed in June 2025 that he had proposed, but Berry did not publicly confirm their engagement until February 2026.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

"I think we will get married just because, out of the people I’ve been married to, this is the person I should have married," Berry told "Today" in June 2025. "And I feel like I should, we should get married, but it’s not because we feel like we have to. I think it’s something that we would like to do just because we want that expression."

Berry was previously married to David Justice from 1993 to 1997, Eric Benét from 2001 to 2005 and Olivier Martinez from 2013 to 2015, though her divorce from Martinez was not fully settled until 2023.

item.title: Bomani Jones baselessly accuses 'White folks' of favoring Josh Allen, while he favors Black quarterbacks
item.description: Bomani Jones accused White people of having a bias toward Josh Allen, claiming they are ready for his "coronation" as the Buffalo Bills' quarterback.
item.content:encoded:
Though it's not even late August, former ESPN host Bomani Jones is already angered by Josh Allen and the White folks.

On his podcast this week, Jones previewed the NFL season by accusing White people of having a bias toward Allen that people of color do not share.

"America's number one rooting project, the Buffalo Bills ... they got him a new stadium. Boy, White folks is so ready for the eventual Josh Allen coronation. And it's not all the White folks, but it's White folks. We ain't got it."

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

Is that so?

His guest, The Ringer writer Diante Lee, nodded along, saying, "It's enough of them [White folks]."

Damn those White folks.

If you were wondering which story, scandal, podcast, or statement Jones and Lee are referring to, you are not alone. I wondered the same thing. Unfortunately, neither specified what proof they have of this supposed racial bias.

OutKick asked both Jones and Lee to explain. Neither has responded as of publication. We will update this story if either does.

But don't expect it.

Bomani Jones has been on this talking point for a while. He has long accused nameless media figures of giving Josh Allen a pass and rooting for him because he is White.

Jones is one of the leading participants in the media-manufactured race war between Allen and Lamar Jackson. As expected, he sides with Jackson. Just last week, he complained that anonymous people — who else? — are putting more pressure on Jackson than Allen this season.

His argument: The Bills kept Allen and gave him a new head coach, so he has no more excuses.

The problem: The Ravens also kept Jackson and gave him a new coach.

Why the double standard? While racially motivated, Jones may not have known that the Ravens fired John Harbaugh and hired Jesse Minter. He often doesn't appear to know the details about the sports he covers, beyond the skin colors of the subjects involved.

EX-ESPN HOST SAYS SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM DESERVED TO BE EJECTED AND PUNISHED — NOT DIJONAI CARRINGTON, WHO CLOTHESLINED HER

Last season, he said Stafford must win a Super Bowl to make the Hall of Fame.

"He's the new Josh Allen," Jones said about Stafford. "He's the least scrutinized No. 1 pick in the history of No. 1 overall picks. If the Rams don't win the Super Bowl, shut this Hall of Fame thing up."

Jones was seemingly unaware that Stafford had already won a Super Bowl just a few years earlier.

He later backtracked, saying Stafford needed to win a second Super Bowl to earn a spot in the Hall of Fame. This argument didn't make much sense either, considering only 13 quarterbacks have won more than one Super Bowl, yet 36 have been enshrined, many of whom have lesser resumes than Stafford.

But the facts didn't matter. Stafford played the Bears that week, and Jones needed to find a way to discredit Stafford and elevate Caleb Williams.

Likewise, he is now arguing that Kyler Murray is a better quarterback than Sam Darnold, who just won a Super Bowl last season.

Are you starting to see a trend?

Bomani is also not a believer in Drake Maye, Fernando Mendoza or Justin Herbert. He does, however, have great faith in Cam Ward, Jayden Daniels and Dak Prescott.

The prediction here is that Jones will prefer Dante Moore over Arch Manning in next year's NFL Draft.

To be clear, Jones understands his audience. His reach is now limited to a niche group of sports fans who want to hear that White people are inferior athletes who have survived only because of White privilege.

Therefore, Jones has lowered himself to arguing with straw men, whom he accuses of favoring Allen and Stafford based on their skin color.

Granted, even his own fans appear tired of the schtick. Here's the top message on his Reddit fan page as of Friday afternoon:

"Bomani has completely lost the juice.

"Today’s episode made me tap out. He has nothing interesting left to say. If he’s going to spend the entire NFL season making the same 5 points about Stafford, Allen, Murray, and Hurts I’ll pass.

"He had a great run but it’s honestly kinda depressing what he’s turned into."

THE LEFT WANTS CAITLIN CLARK, SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM TO SHUT UP AND DRIBBLE WHEN IT COMES TO TRANS SPORTS

The market for racial idolatry in sports media has collapsed. The demand for Jones, Ryan Clark, Jemele Hill, Cari Champion and many others is over. In fact, Jones never had much of an audience anyway. See the ratings for his former shows at ESPN.

Put simply, there is no evidence that White folks are rooting for Josh Allen because he's White. But because Bomani so clearly roots for Black quarterbacks because they are Black, something he has admitted, he assumes everyone else is like him.

Fortunately, most people are not. Most people are not this concerned about the skin colors of the people playing quarterback.

item.title: Trump’s fight over rarely used 18th-century deportation law lives on in latest court clash
item.description: The 5th Circuit dismissed a challenge to Trump's use of the Alien Enemies Act against alleged Tren de Aragua members after all plaintiffs were deported.
item.content:encoded:
The Fifth U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals on Thursday dismissed as moot a challenge to President Donald Trump’s use of the Alien Enemies Act to deport alleged Tren de Aragua members, leaving the legality of his invocation of the 18th-century law unresolved.

The New Orleans-based court said the case became moot after all three Venezuelan plaintiffs, whom the administration alleged were members of Tren de Aragua, had already been removed from the United States under other immigration authorities.

While the Alien Enemies Act dates back hundreds of years, prior to Trump, it was most recently invoked by President Harry Truman in 1946. The law allows the president, under specified wartime or invasion circumstances involving a foreign nation or government, to detain and remove certain non-naturalized individuals of that hostile power.

The Trump administration has argued that Tren de Aragua’s gang activity amounts to an "invasion or predatory incursion" under the law and has sought to use the authority as part of its broader immigration agenda, including efforts to speed the removal of suspected gang members.

DC APPEALS COURT ORDERS JUDGE BOASBERG TO HALT TRUMP CONTEMPT PROBE OVER DEPORTATION FLIGHTS

The Supreme Court previously blocked the administration from removing the detainees under the Alien Enemies Act while the case proceeded, but stopped short of deciding whether Trump had lawfully invoked the statute, sending the dispute back to the Fifth Circuit.

Advancing American Freedom senior legal fellow Bryce Poole described the ruling as a mixed result for the Trump administration.

"The Fifth Circuit's en banc decision in W.M.M. v. Trump represents one step forward, one step sideways for the Trump Administration," Advancing American Freedom senior legal fellow Bryce Poole told Fox News Digital. "Last year, in A.A.R.P. v. Trump, the Supreme Court blocked the removals but declined to decide whether President Trump's invocation of the Alien Enemies Act was lawful, sending that question back to the Fifth Circuit."

Advancing American Freedom is a conservative public policy advocacy organization founded by former Vice President Mike Pence.

"It's a step forward because it vacates the prior ruling that said Trump's invocation was unlawful, leaving the President's AEA powers intact," Poole explained. "It's a step sideways because the court dodged the merits, so the AEA's legality remains a live question the Supreme Court will likely decide — probably in a different case like J.A.V. v. Trump, which has a certified class, so mootness won't apply."

BIDEN JUDGE OVERRULED ON KEY TRUMP IMMIGRATION POLICY

Even though the court declined to rule on the merits, two judges signaled their belief that the president’s use of the law was appropriate in their concurring opinions.

"I agree that this case is moot," Judge James Ho wrote. "But I also agree with the United States that we should address the merits questions directed to us by the Supreme Court — and affirm the President’s actions under the Alien Enemies Act and the Due Process Clause."

"As I’ve also noted, judges are supposed to defer to a President’s declaration of a state of invasion — including the ones issued on January 20, 2025." Ho, a Trump appointee, added. "And if courts must defer when the President treats illegal immigration as an invasion, see id., then a fortiori we must defer when it comes to the narrower question of an invasion by Tren de Aragua."

Ilya Somin, a George Mason law professor and scholar at the libertarian Cato Institute, disagreed strongly with Ho’s rationale.

"If the president could create an 'invasion' simply by claiming that it exists, it would convert dangerous emergency powers that can only be used in extreme circumstances into blank checks the president can invoke any time he wants" he wrote. "That's contrary to the text of the AEA (which limits its use to situations where these circumstances actually exist) and to the text and original meaning of the Constitution."

SUPREME COURT'S LATEST IMMIGRATION RULING WILL CAUSE AMERICANS TO 'DIE AND SUFFER' ATTORNEY WARNS

Judge Andrew Oldham, another Trump appointee, also agreed that the president’s invocation of the Alien Enemies Act was legally sound.

With all 17 active Fifth Circuit judges participating, the court refused a request from the plaintiffs’ lawyers to substitute in new plaintiffs for the men who the Trump administration deported.

Trump’s invocation of the Alien Enemies Act remains legally unresolved following the dismissal, with the court’s actions likely delaying a possible final decision at the Supreme Court.

item.title: Spanish broadcaster allegedly skips Israeli hurdler during introductions at European Athletics Championships
item.description: RTVE anchors appeared to skip Israeli hurdler Omri Shiff during athlete introductions at the European Athletics Championships in Birmingham.
item.content:encoded:
A Spanish national broadcast channel is in hot water following an alleged omission during its coverage of the European Athletics Championships in Birmingham, England this week.

RTVE, a news organization in Spain, was covering a hurdling event that featured athletes from all over the world lining up in their starting positions and staying loose.

As the camera panned to each individual participant, the anchors for RTVE introduced the athletes by name as well the country they represented.

However, when the camera reached Omri Shiff, a hurdler from Israel, both anchors inexplicably averted their attention to another participant who was apparently taking too long to get set.

EXCLUSIVE: ISRAELI PRESIDENT HERZOG BLASTS MAMDANI, PRAISES TRUMP, SOUNDS ALARM ON IRAN

By the time the camera moved off Shiff and onto another athlete from Hungary, the introductions resumed, and the rest of the athletes were once again mentioned by their name and what country they were there to represent.

Even if you don't speak fluent Spanish, you can tell just by their cadence as well as the names being used that Shiff wasn't acknowledged during the athlete intros. You can even hear an audible pause while Shiff is being shown before the male anchor steps in to say something.

GERMAN OFFICIALS WARN ISLAMIST, FAR-LEFT RHETORIC DRIVING SPIKE IN ANTISEMITIC ATTACKS

After the camera moved to the Hungarian participant, the female anchor appeared to laugh and make a quick comment before returning to the athlete introductions.

RTVE issued a public apology in a statement to The Jewish Chronicle, saying, "We sincerely regret not having named all the athletes who appeared on screen during the broadcasts on Teledeporte [sports channel], as happened in the case of the Israeli athlete Omar Shiff.

"This situation was exclusively due to the complexity of the long athletics sessions and the dynamics of live broadcasting – such as trackside commentary or production requirements – and was in no way related to political, ideological or religious reasons.

"Our commitment is to give visibility to every participant, and we work to achieve this in every broadcast. We reiterate our apology to the athlete affected."

The outlet did not respond to requests for comment from OutKick.

item.title: Democratic governor credits Trump for delivering project for Michigan that Biden couldn't get over finish line
item.description: Democratic Michigan Gov. Gretchen Whitmer said Trump helped her land a new F-15EX Eagle II fighter jet mission at Selfridge Air National Guard Base.
item.content:encoded:
Democratic Michigan Gov. Gretchen Whitmer said Thursday President Donald Trump has helped her deliver for the state, pointing to a specific fighter jet mission she tried to secure during the Biden administration but couldn't.

Whitmer spoke to Newsom on his podcast, "This is Gavin Newsom," and said she needed to figure out how to conduct herself after the 2024 presidential election because her state had voted for Trump again.

Newsom noted Whitmer had visited the White House, and the pair both agreed a working relationship with the president was "part of the job."

"I've gotten some really good stuff done. Honestly," she told Newsom. "I got a fighter mission at Selfridge Air National Guard Base, and I tried to get that done under the Biden administration, couldn't get over the finish line, but I got it done with him. So, that's a huge deal to Michigan."

PROGRESSIVE PRAISE FOR TRUMP AS WARREN BACKS PUSH TO CURB DEFENSE CONTRACTOR CEO PAYOUTS

Former President Joe Biden's office didn't immediately respond to a request for comment.

Whitmer appeared to be referring to Mission Next, which will replace the retiring A-10 Warthog aircraft based at Selfridge Air National Guard Base in Michigan with 21 brand-new F-15EX Eagle II fighter jets. The mission is part of a modernization plan for the National Guard Base, according to the National Guard's website, which includes construction and infrastructure upgrades that will create jobs and new training opportunities.

Trump shared details of the new fighter jet mission in April 2025 during a speech to National Guard members at the Michigan base for an event commemorating his 100th day in office.

"Fresh off the line. That means they are brand new," Trump said at the time. "They've never been anywhere. This is where they're going to be for a long time. And I saw one of them, flew over my head, and I said, ‘What the hell is that?’ That plane has serious power. So, this is the best there is anywhere in the world, the F-15EX Eagle II. This will keep Selfridge at the cutting edge of Northern American air power."

JD VANCE UNCOVERS THE HIDDEN WHITE HOUSE DRESS CODE PRESIDENT TRUMP EXPECTS FROM HIS INNER CIRCLE

"While Joe Biden’s weak policies neglected our military, President Trump saved Selfridge Air National Guard Base, a crucial pillar of North American air defense; rebuilt our military; and restored readiness and lethality to our U.S. Armed Forces," White House spokeswoman Olivia Wales told Fox News Digital Friday.

"With President Trump as commander in chief, the United States Military will continue to lead the world in power, prestige, and might," Wales continued. "President Trump proudly won the state of Michigan in 2024, and will continue to deliver on his promises for all Michiganders."

Whitmer said during the podcast conversation with Newsom that she knew how to work with people who weren't her best friends, even if she didn't like it. 

The Michigan governor went viral in April 2025 for attempting to hide her face while photos were being taken during an Oval Office meeting with the president. She explained the moment days later and said she just didn't want her picture taken.

"I don’t want my picture taken, that’s all it was. I kind of wished I hadn’t put my folder up in front of my face, but whatever. You know I was there … I just wrote a book about learning to laugh at yourself, so I’m pretty good at it. We all have our moments," Whitmer said.

Trump notably praised Whitmer at the time, calling her a "very good person," even though the pair have traded barbs in the past.

item.title: Trump claims AOC may run for president as far-left Dems back away from extreme policy
item.description: President Donald Trump said Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez and progressive Democrats are all trying to disavow their defund police and sanctuary cities stances.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump said Friday that far-left Democrats like Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., are now trying to distance themselves from some of the radical positions they once championed, noting he believes she may be after a 2028 bid for the White House.

In an interview with Fox News correspondent Alexis McAdams, Trump was asked about Ocasio-Cortez's perceived shift away from her earlier calls to defund police departments and other soft-on-crime policies.

"If you really look at it, they're all saying the same thing," Trump said of progressive Democrats. "They're all trying to disavow themselves from what they said about crime and, well, they're saying, ‘We love sanctuary cities.’"

When asked directly whether he thinks AOC is positioning herself for a presidential bid, Trump said he thinks AOC will run.

The congresswoman has refused to rule out a run for president, but she hasn't looked past November's midterm elections.

ALEXANDRIA OCASIO-CORTEZ SHRUGS OFF PAST 'DEFUND THE POLICE' COMMENTS, JOKING 'WOKE 1 WAS CRAZY'

During an interview with ABC's "This Week" on Sunday, the congresswoman attempted to dismiss the extreme rhetoric of the so-called "Woke 1" era.

The term is used by some progressive politicians to describe the pandemic-era social justice activism and far-left political rhetoric in 2019 and 2020, when some called for the defunding of law enforcement agencies, the abolition of police and prisons, the elimination of cash bail, open borders and unchecked migration.

Trump said some Democrats are now trying to distance themselves from sanctuary cities, which generally don't cooperate with federal immigration authorities.

"I think you're going to see sanctuary cities start to end, because sanctuary cities are a disaster. And somebody like her, she was big for sanctuary cities," Trump said of Ocasio-Cortez. "They cause crime.

"That's when it all started. No cash bail," he added. "Somebody kills somebody, and they just say, ‘All right, go ahead and come back in two weeks.’"

During AOC's ABC interview, Jonathan Karl briefly pressed the congresswoman, a member of the New York chapter of the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA), on radical comments made by fellow socialist and Wisconsin gubernatorial candidate Francesca Hong in 2020 and 2021.

"I have a local city councilman that has this saying, 'Woke 1 was crazy,'" Ocasio-Cortez said while grinning. "And I think that what’s important is that we have to assess what a candidate is saying now."

Ocasio-Cortez's office did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

item.title: Dolphins consultant Troy Aikman will be limited in MNF role like Raiders minority owner Tom Brady is on Fox
item.description: Troy Aikman must follow the same NFL restrictions placed on Tom Brady after adding a consultant role with the Miami Dolphins this offseason.
item.content:encoded:
Troy Aikman, who this offseason added an informal consultant role with the Miami Dolphins to his work on ESPN's Monday Night Football telecast, has been told he must abide by restrictions that have been on Tom Brady for a couple of years.

The NFL confirmed to Fox News Digital a report by Front Office Sports on Friday that Aikman must limit some of his access to clubs as part of his preparation for games.

Those limitations were initially placed on Brady when he joined Fox Sports.

TOM BRADY SENDS CLEAR MESSAGE TO RAIDERS ROOKIE FERNANDO MENDOZA: EARN YOUR OPPORTUNITY

"The same parameters that pertained to Tom last season will continue this year and also will apply to Troy," NFL spokesman Brian McCarthy said in a statement to Fox News Digital.

"Both may attend production meetings virtually but will have no access to practice facilities or practices.

"They may conduct interviews outside team facilities with football personnel and players. They could conduct the interview at the team hotel in an area separate from other football personnel."

One more thing:

"They could broadcast games involving their own club," McCarthy added.

Aikman has been the lead color commentator for "Monday Night Football" alongside Joe Buck since 2022 but this offseason he was added to the Dolphins hierarchy when ownership brought him in to help in the general manager and head coach search that eventually led to the hiring of Jon-Eric Sullivan and Jeff Hafley.

Hafley thanked Aikman at his introductory press conference for being part of the search committee that chose him as head coach. Sullivan clarified that Aikman is kept "in the fold" as an active resource, though with a distinct boundary regarding roster construction.

It is clear, however, that Aikman provides his insights to ownership and other club leadership when he deems necessary and those are welcome. At least some of those insights are obviously gathered from his broadcast role connections.

Aikman's role in Miami doesn't seem quite as formal as that of Brady, who is the No. 1 analyst on Fox broadcasts and also a minority owner of the Las Vegas Raiders. But the NFL is treating both the same now.

The league has been pleased with how Brady has balanced his dual roles and stayed within guidelines. It has no concerns that Brady, previously, and Aikman, in future, will pose a conflict of interest for any team.

"There have been no issues with Tom over the last two seasons. It is up to the coaches and clubs what they share with him," McCarthy said. "If they share information they shouldn’t, then that’s on them."

Interestingly, the information Aikman has shared so far probably has hurt the Dolphins rather than helped.

During an interview earlier this month on the "Dallas Dialogue with Dale" show, Aikman pointed out that the Dolphins are not going to be a good team in 2026.

Everyone pretty much knew that already, but the problem is both Hafley and Sullivan have been working to get out the message that they want to win. That they aren't tanking this season.

(The Dolphins tanked the 2019 season by trading and releasing multiple big-name players in hopes of gaining a high NFL Draft pick in the first round of the 2020 draft. It sort of worked, although coach Brian Flores didn't go along with the plan and milked five wins out of a roster constructed to lose).

Anyway, Aikman apparently didn't get the memo from Hafley and Sullivan, who don't want their players and fans to think winning isn't a priority this season.

"The Dolphins are not expected to be very good this year," Aikman said. "They're getting out of cap hell, so there's no Monday night game with the Dolphins this year."

The Dolphins indeed do not play on Monday Night Football this season. But perhaps they would be smart to speak with Aikman about getting with the company line.

item.title: Minor League team rolls out 'Nothing Night' with no music, videos, or public address announcements
item.description: The Sugar Land Space Cowboys will strip away walk-up music, Jumbotron videos, and between-innings promotions for their first "Nothing Night" on Aug. 18.
item.content:encoded:
Minor league baseball is known for its theme nights, promotional giveaways, and on-field antics that keep the fans entertained all game long.

But at a time when this has become the norm, some want their baseball without a side of music blaring and the mascot doing donuts in the outfield on an ATV.

And that's exactly what the Sugar Land Space Cowboys, the Triple-A affiliate of the Houston Astros, will do on Aug. 18 when they host their first-ever "Nothing Night."

"One of our executives back then had worked in Lake Elsinore, who did this as the Lake Elsinore Storm back in, I believe, 2008, and they went way extreme for it," the team's play-by-play announcer and manager of media relations Garrett Greene said. "It was like free admission, but there were no concession stands, and the bathrooms were locked.

"And we were like, 'Let's not go that far with this.'"

So, bathrooms and concessions will be available, but don't expect usual staples like walk-up music, videos on the Jumbotron, or games on the field between innings. This means that the crowd's attention has only one place to go: on the baseball game taking place directly in front of them.

"There are some times where it's like, 'Hey, it would be fun to just show up and just have a nice, easy, relaxing game where the focus is entirely on the field,'" Greene said. "As the broadcaster, the game's normally the focus for me, but it's kind of nice that for one night we said, 'Hey, let's just strip everything else away. It's just one night and show kind of what baseball is.'

"If we take away all the crazy sound effects, music, in-between innings promotions, giveaways, and just make it, 'Hey, just show up, and the game is right there in front of you, and that's the most important thing for the night."

The Space Cowboys (what a killer name, by the way) will take on the Oklahoma City Comets on Nothing Night, and while you won't see any frills, all the necessities for a modern baseball game will be on hand.

FIRST ON FOX — The Kennedy Center Board of Trustees wants to name the famed arts institution’s grounds the "President Donald J. Trump Plaza," one of several new ways the board is seeking to honor the president as the center moves ahead with a sweeping renovation, Fox News Digital has learned.

The board also wants the words "Endowed by the Trump Kennedy Center Fund" inscribed on the building once the fund reaches a $100 million endowment, according to information obtained by Fox News Digital.

KENNEDY CENTER BOARD MEMBER KNOCKS SEN WHITEHOUSE FOR IGNORING INVITES AS DEM FEUDS WITH TRUMP-RUN LANDMARK

The board’s resolution calls for an inscription below the name of the center reading, "The John F. Kennedy Memorial Center for the Performing Arts Restored and Renovated by President Donald J. Trump."

item.title: Judge’s Harvard antisemitism ruling sends Trump Justice Department back to drawing board
item.description: The Justice Department says it disagrees with the ruling dismissing its Title VI antisemitism case against Harvard University and is assessing next steps.
item.content:encoded:
The Justice Department is planning its next move after a federal judge in Boston dismissed its case accusing Harvard University of repeatedly turning a "blind eye" to antisemitism on campus.

"We disagree with the ruling and are assessing next steps," Assistant Attorney General for the Civil Rights Division Harmeet Dhillon said in a statement. 

"The Civil Rights Division has an extensive and active portfolio of antisemitism enforcement, including indictments, prosecutions, settlements and investigations across the country."

Judge Richard Stearns, who was appointed by President Bill Clinton, dismissed the Trump administration's lawsuit against the Ivy League school Thursday, determining the incidents of antisemitism were too isolated to establish a pattern showing that the school remained in violation of federal civil rights law after the federal government issued its complaint.

DOJ SUES UCLA OVER ALLEGED ‘JUDENREIN’ CONDITIONS DURING ANTI-ISRAEL ENCAMPMENT

"Without diminishing any concern arising from these occurrences, the court finds them, singly and collectively, to be too isolated and episodic to support a plausible inference that any institutionalized noncompliance with Title VI persists at Harvard to this day," Stearns wrote.

The Justice Department filed its lawsuit against Harvard March 20, 2026, after a wave of anti-Israel protests that erupted on college campuses nationwide after Hamas’ Oct. 7, 2023, attack on Israel and the ensuing war in Gaza.

At Harvard, protests during the 2023-24 school year included repeated occupations of libraries and other campus buildings and a weekslong encampment in Harvard Yard. Jewish students reported being harassed, intimidated and excluded from campus spaces. 

The Justice Department alleged that Harvard violated Title VI by failing to protect Jewish and Israeli students from harassment despite complaints to university leaders about the conduct.

But Stearns said the Justice Department referred to only three antisemitic incidents on Harvard's campus during the following school year that the school had allegedly failed to address.

UCLA STUDENT COUNCIL CONDEMNS CAMPUS EVENT WITH FORMER ISRAELI HOSTAGE

Those incidents included protesters allegedly breaching barricades outside an event featuring former Israeli Prime Minister Naftali Bennett, a Harvard employee allegedly removing posters of Israeli hostages and more than 60 masked protesters staging a "die-in" outside Widener Library, where they chanted, "We will honor all our martyrs."

Stearns did not rule on whether Harvard had violated Title VI during the height of the campus unrest. Instead, his decision focused on whether the Justice Department had sufficiently alleged that violations continued after the government formally put Harvard on notice.

The Trump administration sent Harvard a warning letter June 30, 2025, saying the school had violated Title VI over its response to antisemitism on campus.

Under the statute, the government is required to notify a recipient of a violation and try to resolve it voluntarily before taking enforcement action.

DOJ SPRINGS ANTISEMITISM REVIEW ON BLUE STATE COLLEGE AFTER 'LEBANESE RESISTANCE' FUNDRAISER

In his dismissal, Stearns said the Trump administration's amended June 2026 complaint did not identify any incidents in which Harvard failed to address antisemitism after the government sent its warning letter.

"The Government provided the requisite notice underlying this action on June 30, 2025," Stearns wrote. "As noted above, the Amended Complaint is devoid of any factual allegations plausibly establishing that any events that might be construed as evidence of noncompliance occurred after June 30, 2025."

Stearns also rejected the Trump administration's allegation that Harvard University's failure to cooperate with every demand in the federal government's proposed voluntary agreement showed that the school was not in compliance with Title VI.

"Harvard’s refusal to follow every specific demand from the administration wasn’t enough, because the legal question was whether Harvard was complying with Title VI — not whether Harvard was doing exactly what the administration told it to do," Stearns wrote.

The dismissal comes as the Trump administration pursues two lawsuits against the University of California over alleged discrimination against Jewish and Israeli students, faculty and staff at UCLA.

Fox News Digital reached out to Harvard University for comment.

item.title: Alzheimer's risk may be 35% lower with common menopause treatment, study finds
item.description: A Stanford study found estrogen-only menopausal hormone therapy linked to 35% lower Alzheimer's pathology and 39% lower dementia odds in women.
item.content:encoded:
Women who used estrogen-only menopausal hormone therapy (MHT) were less likely to develop Alzheimer’s-related brain changes or dementia, according to a large Stanford study published Aug. 12 in Neurology.

The researchers analyzed post-mortem data from 21,462 participants, comparing 258 women who reported estrogen-only MHT use with approximately 2,701 women who reported no MHT use.

The researchers examined the brains for signs of Alzheimer’s disease, including amyloid plaques, neurofibrillary tangles and amyloid-plaque density. Plaques and tangles are two hallmark brain changes associated with the common dementia.

ALZHEIMER'S BLOOD TESTS MAY PREDICT SYMPTOMS YEARS IN ADVANCE, BUT EXPERTS URGE CAUTION

The women who took estrogen-only therapy — most of whom had likely undergone hysterectomies — were found to have a 35% lower chance of Alzheimer’s pathology and 39% lower odds of dementia over a lifetime.

Among some living participants, estrogen-only users also performed better on memory testing and were better able to function independently, the study found. Biomarkers in blood and cerebrospinal fluid supported these results.

The participants averaged 70 years of age.

Recent research indicates that menopausal hormone therapy may offer greater benefits when started during or shortly after menopause, the researchers noted.

HOW EATING HABITS COULD INFLUENCE PARKINSON’S DISEASE RISK, ACCORDING TO EXPERTS

Because the women in the study were generally older when they began treatment, the results may actually understate the potential benefits of earlier therapy.

These findings appear to contradict prior studies that linked menopausal hormone therapy to increased dementia risk.

"Estrogen has well-described neuroprotective effects in animal models," co-author Jennifer Bruno, PhD, an instructor in psychiatry and behavioral sciences, told Fox News Digital.

"Estrogen plays a role in shifting amyloid toward the non-amyloidogenic pathway and promoting tau dephosphorylation — both amyloid and tau are hallmarks of Alzheimer’s disease."

DAILY EATING HABIT LINKED TO BETTER BRAIN HEALTH IN OLDER ADULTS, NEW RESEARCH SUGGESTS

"Additionally, estrogen supports synaptic plasticity, reduces neuroinflammation and supports blood brain barrier integrity. So, finding less AD pathology in estrogen-only users was consistent with this mechanism."

Memory can be impacted by many different conditions, which means clinical diagnoses can sometimes be unreliable, the researchers noted.

"Although there’s been great progress with bloodborne and cerebrospinal fluid biomarkers, they don’t tell you the amount and precise location of the brain damage," said senior author Hadi Hosseini, Ph.D., an associate professor of psychiatry and behavioral sciences at Stanford.

"By looking where the actual damage is done — the brain — you can see where the Alzheimer’s-associated defining features are and how many of them are there."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

The study did have some limitations, according to the researchers. As it was observational, it could only show an association but could prove that the hormone therapy reduced Alzheimer’s risk.

"It’s possible that women who used hormone therapy differed from non-users in ways we couldn't fully measure, such as baseline health status or engagement with healthcare," Hosseini told Fox News Digital. "We worked hard to adjust for known confounders and to account for who does and doesn't come to autopsy, but observational data can only take you so far."

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

Alzheimer’s disease is the leading cause of dementia among older adults, with women comprising about two-thirds of diagnoses.

While the study findings don’t change current clinical recommendations, Hosseini said they highlight the need for well-designed clinical trials to confirm these observations and to determine whether menopausal hormone therapy has a protective cognitive effect.

"These results add meaningful, first-of-their-kind pathological evidence to a genuinely controversial area — but they are a signal for further study, not a reason to start or stop MHT for brain health," Bruno added.

"We need prospective, biomarker-based trials that follow women before, during and after menopause to understand the effects of MHT on brain health."

The study was funded by the National Institutes of Health.

item.title: Paul Pelosi absent from first court appearance on hit-and-run charge in Napa County crash case
item.description: Paul Pelosi did not appear in court Friday, and his attorney entered a not guilty plea on his behalf in a Napa County hit-and-run case stemming from a July 3 crash.
item.content:encoded:
Paul Pelosi did not appear in a Napa County courtroom Friday for his first scheduled court appearance on a misdemeanor hit-and-run charge, and an attorney entered a not guilty plea on his behalf.

Pelosi, 86, the husband of former House Speaker Nancy Pelosi, D-Calif., was represented by attorney Amanda Bevins in Napa County Superior Court, according to the California Post.

Bevins declined to comment when reached by Fox News Digital Friday.

PAUL PELOSI, 86, FACES A HIT-AND-RUN CHARGE AFTER STRIKING A PARKED CAR IN NAPA COUNTY: SHERIFF'S OFFICE

The court date came nearly a month after the Napa County District Attorney's Office formally charged Pelosi with misdemeanor hit-and-run and an infraction for an unsafe turning movement stemming from a July 3 crash.

According to a criminal complaint previously obtained by Fox News Digital, Pelosi allegedly struck and damaged a parked Tesla while driving a burgundy Maserati convertible before leaving without attempting to identify the Tesla's owner or provide the information required under California law.

Deputies later located Pelosi roughly a half-mile away, where he allegedly told officers he had intended to return to the crash site, according to the complaint.

Prosecutors contend those actions formed the basis for the misdemeanor charge and accompanying traffic infraction.

FLORIDA MAN ARRESTED FOR DUI AFTER TROOPERS ALLEGEDLY FIND 34 OPEN ALCOHOL CONTAINERS IN VEHICLE

The district attorney's office said last month that it does not typically issue news releases announcing misdemeanor hit-and-run cases involving only property damage but made an exception because of the "significant public and media interest" surrounding Pelosi.

Pelosi, a venture capitalist who has long maintained a residence in Napa County, was allegedly driving the Maserati at the time of the collision. The complaint did not indicate whether anyone else was in the car.

The case marks Pelosi's second high-profile traffic-related legal matter in Napa County in recent years.

In 2022, Pelosi pleaded guilty to misdemeanor DUI after a separate crash in the county. He was sentenced to probation, ordered to pay restitution and fines, required to complete a DUI education program and ordered to install an ignition interlock device.

The July case also brought renewed attention to Pelosi's driving history. The New York Times reported last month that Pelosi has received driving infractions in four Bay Area counties in recent years, including San Francisco, Marin, San Mateo and Napa.

According to the Times, the infractions included speeding, driving the wrong way on a one-way street, using a cellphone without a hands-free device and failing to stop at a red light.

The Times also reported that Pelosi was driving during a 1957 crash in San Mateo County that killed his 19-year-old brother. A jury later cleared Pelosi of wrongdoing in that crash.

Fox News Digital's Jasmine Baehr contributed to this report.

item.title: Marco Rubio's perfect weekend will make the left faint, Danica Patrick enjoys the view & angry Mike Vrabel!
item.description: Marco Rubio perfectly describes the ideal fall football weekend while Mike Vrabel rips his kicker after three missed field goals in Patriots preseason.
item.content:encoded:
'Nightcaps' is a daily column that catches you up on the biggest sports, news and culture stories you may have missed while pretending to do work at your desk. It runs Monday–Friday on OutKick.com.

Middle Friday of August. We're here. We're in the thick of it, folks.

We had football last night. We have football tonight. We have football tomorrow. Sure, none of it counts and most of the good players are in street clothes on the bench, but whatever.

It's our first kinda-sorta football weekend since early January. A tuneup, of sorts. A test run. It's preseason for us fans, too. We have to knock the rust off as well, and we don't have a lot of time to do it.

Two weeks. That's all that separates us from an actual college football Saturday. Week 0 is 15 days away. That means you — yes, YOU — have this weekend and next weekend to get the summer chores DONE. Finish cleaning the yard, and clearing out the garage. Hang the pictures. Paint the walls.

Do whatever you need to do over these next two weekends, because the end is, mercifully, in sight.

Let's roll.

Welcome to a Friday Nightcaps — the one where Danica Patrick enjoys the view during her European summer vacation.

What else? I've got Marco Rubio perfectly describing the perfect fall weekend (to a T), an American home run into a cornfield, and I'm thinking the Patriots' kicker better spend the weekend combing through the classifieds, because Mike Vrabel didn't sound thrilled after last night's game.

Good to have angry Vrabel back after a ... humbling ... offseason.

Grab you whatever you need to get you through the final few hours of a work week, and settle in for a Friday 'Cap!

No hemming and hawing today. It's a Friday and we've all got things to do. We'll start with Marco, because that above clip is just perfect.

Seriously. It's the perfect weekend, and one we all will be striving for in about three weeks. It's the one we've been dreaming about since last January. Really, last December.

"The day would actually start much earlier. The greatest show on television today in America is 'College GameDay.' Great show. Starts around 10 or 11, and that leads you to noon, and then the noon game, and then there’s a 3:30 game," he said.

"You could start at 10:00 AM on Saturday, you know, run the whole college football day, sleep for a few hours, then you wake up and then you’re into NFL Gameday. Then you’ve got the 1:00 game, the 4:00 game, the NBC game that night.

"That is an incredible weekend, in my opinion, in my view."

Bingo. He nailed it. Put aside politics for a minute. This is objectively the best possible weekend for the next few months.

Mix in a few monster parlays on Saturday and Sunday, some fantasy football sweating, and a date with Scott Hanson on the RedZone channel, and buddy, you are SET.

We're almost back, folks. Hang tight!

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

Five more Sundays. Two more Saturdays. It's all coming together.

In the meantime, of course, we have preseason football. We had a six-pack of games last night, and six more tonight.

Yes, I know — "Preseason football STINKS! Just get me to the regular season." I get it. Trust me, I do. But, this is the time of year for evaluation.

You don't know whatcha have ... till you know whatcha have.

And what the New England Patriots have ... is a kicker problem:

Amazing stuff. I forgot how likable Vrabel was this offseason, which is understandable. Adultery will do that to a person's reputation.

The guy doesn't mince words.

"Andy missed a couple field goals today, what was your message to him?"

"Three. I don't have a message. We're expected to make them. That's pro football."

Okeedokee, coach. Good luck today, Andy!

OK, let's rapid-fire this Friday class into a big Friday night. First up? Let's rewind to the very beginning of last night's Patriots game and check in, again, with Mike Vrabel:

Lordy. What a toss! I hate the Patriots, by the way, so I don't love having this much Pats content in a Friday class. But fair is fair. I don't make the #content, I just write about it.

Next? Might as well stay on the gridiron and check in with George Kittle and Mac Jones to see how they spent their preseason opener:

Anyone here done smelling salts? Admittedly, I have not. I've always wanted to try, though. I'm a little surprised they never came up when I was playing. Feels like a missed opportunity.

They always look like a wild little ride to me. Let me know!

Next? Here's the best baseball stat of the day on the way out:

Amazing. Is there a greater, more American feeling than launching a home run into a cornfield? You'd be hard-pressed to find one.

And how about those NAMES on that list? Anyone here remember Andy Pafko's home run during the first televised baseball game on CBS? I doubt it.

Pafko's better known for being the player standing haplessly in left field during Bobby Thomson's "shot heard 'round the world" in 1951:

Baseball fans fume at MLB's 'Field of Dreams' game decision, reporter Tricia Whitaker has a boat day & LLWS!

Didn't think we'd end the week with a Bobby Thomson YouTube video, but that's why this class wins awards. We zig when they zag!

OK, that's it for today — and this week. Good work, everyone. Happy first kinda-sorta football weekend of the season.

Danica Patrick takes us into it.

Did Marco nail the weekend? Email me at Zach.Dean@OutKick.com.

item.title: Ex-ABC News correspondent claims network overhauled his COVID lab leak report after sending copy to Fauci
item.description: Terry Moran claims ABC News sent his COVID lab leak script to Anthony Fauci, resulting in a piece he says was censored beyond all recognition.
item.content:encoded:
Ex-ABC News correspondent Terry Moran made an explosive claim this week about his former employer and how it allegedly overhauled a report he led on the COVID lab leak theory after running it first by Dr. Anthony Fauci.

In an interview published Friday by "The Fifth Column" podcast, Moran recalled a time he said he felt the "heavy hand of censorship" at the Disney-owned network.

Moran said in early 2021, he had seen discussions from "smart and serious" people online floating the possibility that COVID had leaked from a lab and that ABC's "Nightline" allowed him to pursue a story about the theory.

Moran recalled talking to various scientists and Trump administration officials in a piece that he said did not make any conclusive claims but nevertheless "laid it out."

FAUCI'S DIARY SHOWS HE FED QUESTIONS TO JOURNALISTS, BUILT FRIENDSHIPS WITH MEDIA FIGURES

"We broke a little news that that lab had been funded by the Chinese military, despite the 'Bat Lady' [Chinese virologist Shi Zhengli] saying no, it hadn't... And we kind of laid it out," Moran said. "And at the end of the day, my own personal feeling was, you know, it's probably a little bit more likely it's natural. But if you told me it had leaked from the lab, fine. It's probably not cooked up. It's probably not a ‘Frankenvirus.’"

"And the day that it's supposed to air, it gets reviewed, and it comes back to me, and it is incomprehensible," Moran continued. "And I had never been angrier. I'm in the booth–"

"Are these lawyers?" podcast co-host Michael Moynihan asked.

"Lawyers, standards and, I was told, Fauci," Moran responded. "And I said, 'I can't do this.' And they're going to air and it's a 15-minute piece or whatever. And I'm cursing and screaming in the the booth."

TOP 4 EXPLOSIVE MOMENTS FROM CIA WHISTLEBLOWER'S TESTIMONY ON ALLEGED COVID-19 LAB LEAK COVER-UP

"And this is day of?" co-host Matt Welch followed.

"Day of air," Moran said. "And I am just absolutely livid, beside myself. And I'm usually — I try to be a good colleague that way. It's important to be respectful of somebody on the other end of that mic taking it in in New York and the editor... I have never watched that story and never want to, because it wasn't mine, I didn't think, and most importantly because it was incomprehensible. They had put so many caveats in there, and it was so legalized."

"So they took the story that you did and either sent a copy of the transcript or a copy of the video to Anthony Fauci?" Moynihan then asked.

"It would've been the script — that's what I was told. I don't know if that's true personally, but I was told that," Moran answered.

In the two-part segment that aired in June 2021, Moran's segment put a spotlight on the debate over the origins of COVID. While he did interview Jamie Metzl, then a member of the World Health Organization's committee on human genome editing who had been outspoken about a potential leak from the Wuhan Institute of Virology, Metzl was outnumbered by other medical experts Moran interviewed who rejected the theory. Additionally, the segment included interviews of ABC News medical unit producer Sony Salzman and investigative reporter Sasha Pezenik, who also poured cold water on the lab leak.

FAUCI'S NEWLY RELEASED COVID DIARIES REVEAL BIZARRE FIXATION ON FAME AS PANDEMIC DEATHS MOUNTED

Moran, who exited the network in 2025, went on to denounce the "demonization" of Fauci, calling it wrong and labeling him a public servant who did his best.

Neither Moran, Fauci, nor ABC News responded to Fox News Digital's requests for comment. Fox News Digital also sent an inquiry to the White House.

Fauci has resurfaced in recent weeks following the revelations from his diary published by Sen. Rand Paul, R-Ky., that put a spotlight on how his private thoughts about COVID often contradicted what he said publicly, including about public health guidelines.

The diary also revealed his behind-the-scenes chumminess with numerous media figures, including CNN anchors Jake Tapper and Dana Bash, NBC's Andrea Mitchell and ABC's George Stephanopoulos.

Earlier this month, Senate Republicans on the Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee voted to hold Fauci in contempt of Congress after he pleaded the fifth 111 times during last month's hearing, accusing Paul of leading a crusade to imprison him. A criminal referral was made to the Department of Justice.

The lab leak theory has since been embraced by multiple U.S. government agencies in recent years as the most likely origin of the COVID pandemic, including the CIA, the FBI and the Department of Energy. Many scientists continue to hold to the so-called "natural origin" theory and the topic continues to be hotly debated.

item.title: Houston police shoot gunman who indiscriminately fired on vehicles, injuring a mother and daughter
item.description: A gunman opened fire on passing cars in Houston, wounding a woman and her daughter before three officers and a state trooper shot the suspect.
item.content:encoded:
A gunman who indiscriminately opened fire on passing cars in Houston, striking three people, including a woman and her daughter, was shot by responding police officers, authorities said.

The shooting unfolded at about 11 a.m., when officers responded to reports of someone firing at cars along Wayside Drive. When they arrived, police found a man with a gun, the Houston Police Department said.

The officers commanded the man to drop the weapon. At some point, three officers and a trooper with the Texas Department of Public Safety opened fire on the suspect.

CHICAGO OFFICERS WOUNDED IN TRAFFIC STOP SHOOTOUT AS HOLIDAY WEEKEND LEAVES 3 DEAD, 16 INJURED

The accused gunman was shot multiple times and taken to a hospital. No officers were injured.

"He was standing in the median right here," a witness told KRIV-TV. "He was just shooting at cars coming down Wayside. He didn’t care who was coming which way. He didn’t care who he was shooting at. He didn’t care if there were kids in the car."

Among the targeted vehicles was a car carrying a mother and her daughter, both of whom were struck by gunfire, police said. A third person traveling in a second vehicle was also shot.

SHOOTING NEAR ICE DETENTION FACILITY IN AURORA, COLORADO, LEAVES 1 INJURED, PERSON DETAINED

An occupant in a third vehicle managed to escape unharmed.

The witness, who identified himself only as David, said he and his coworkers tried to stop cars from traveling toward the gunman.

The suspect has not been publicly identified, and a motive for the shooting has not been disclosed.

The incident is being investigated by the Houston Police Department and Texas Rangers.

item.title: Army identifies 2 pilots killed in Apache helicopter crash near Fort Hood during training exercise
item.description: Fort Hood identified the two pilots killed in the AH-64E Apache helicopter crash during a training exercise that sparked a wildfire near Salado, Texas.
item.content:encoded:
The U.S. Army's Fort Hood has identified the two pilots who died during a training exercise Wednesday involving an AH-64E Apache helicopter near Salado, Texas.

Fort Hood identified the fallen soldiers as Chief Warrant Officer 2 Deontre T. Huey and Warrant Officer Seth L. Olmstead.

"Our hearts and deepest condolences are with the families of the Soldiers we lost Wednesday," Lt. Gen. Kevin D. Admiral, III Armored Corps and Fort Hood commanding general, said in a statement the Army released Friday.

"The Army is a family, and a tragedy like this is felt throughout our formations and our community."

ARMY IDS 2 VICTIMS KILLED IN JORDAN AIR BASE ATTACK; TRUMP: IRAN WILL PAY 'MANY TIMES OVER'

Huey entered the Army as a motor transport operator in 2014 and was assigned to Bravo Company, 1st Battalion, 227th Aviation Regiment, 1st Air Cavalry Brigade, 1st Cavalry Division in February 2022. The 34-year-old was from Killeen, Texas.

Olmstead entered the Army in January 2023 as a warrant officer candidate and was assigned to the unit in October 2025. The 25-year-old was a native of Belton, Texas.

"In the difficult days ahead, our priority is to ensure these families and our Soldiers have the care and support they need," Admiral said. "We are making all appropriate resources available to those affected by this loss."

The soldiers died when their helicopter crashed into a field near Salado, roughly 30 minutes from Fort Hood. The crash sparked a wildfire in the area which necessitated a large emergency response.

The Army is investigating the crash.

"A safety investigation team from the U.S. Army Combat Readiness Center in Fort Rucker, Alabama, arrived Aug. 13 and will lead the safety investigation of the mishap," Fort Hood added in the statement.

Fox News Digital contacted the U.S. Army for further comment.

Fox News Digital's Stepheny Price contributed to this report.
